# External spend guarantee assessment

**Decision: real provider execution stays `REAL_PILOT_BLOCKED`.** The SQLite ledger is a local concurrency and recovery control. It cannot constrain invoices generated by other processes or credentials, and provider usage dashboards are not synchronous admission controls.

## Control assessment

| Provider control | Published behavior | Classification for a bounded pilot | Evidence still required |
|---|---|---|---|
| OpenAI project/organization hard spend limit | A hard-limit option is available, but enforcement is not instantaneous and tracked spend may slightly exceed the configured amount. Limits are monthly, not experiment-scoped. | Enforced control with delay; not a hard per-run cap. | Dedicated project and service-account credential; org/project limit, model access, effective period, other users/processes, and actual propagation behavior. |
| Anthropic organization/workspace spend limits | Organization monthly spend limits and rate limits are documented. No settings, account scope, or workspace behavior for this project was inspected. | Unknown for this account; monthly aggregate control is not a per-run guarantee. | Account-specific org/workspace boundaries, limit configuration, enforcement and reporting delay, shared credentials, and model access. |
| Gemini project cap | Project caps are experimental; billing-data delay can permit overage for around ten minutes. Tier billing caps aggregate at billing scope and are not a dedicated run cap. | Delayed/advisory for strict run admission; not a hard per-run cap. | Dedicated project and credentials, linked billing-account scope, current tier and cap, other linked projects, and measured cap behavior. |
| Local SQLite reservation | Atomic against this run's local manifest and fenced claims; preserves uncertain exposure after invocation. | Local enforcement only. | Does not control provider charges outside this process/database or prove provider invoices. |
| Provider usage/cost response | Parsed when supplied by the provider/LiteLLM. | Post-call observation, not pre-call cap. | Invoice reconciliation and complete billable-category semantics. |

No payment method, provider console, API key, account endpoint, or billing setting was inspected or changed. No provider call was made.

## Pilot exposure and unbounded cases

The prepared pilot has 10 planned samples, two arms, 20 primary requests, no retries, no fallback, concurrency 1, temperature 0, and 256 configured generation tokens. The example run budget is USD 2.00 and per-request cap USD 0.10. Those are project configuration values, not an externally guaranteed maximum.

The current provider price/model/context documentation alone does not establish a complete request bill bound. Input token counting is not verified as an enforceable upper bound on the exact transmitted messages and billable framing. A reservation can also remain uncertain if a process is cancelled or crashes after invocation intent. Another process sharing an account or key can spend concurrently. Delayed billing enforcement or reconciliation can occur after the local run completes. Retries or fallback can multiply exposure if later approved; current prepared plan disables them.

The runner's default token counter is `UNKNOWN`; the capability registry marks full billable coverage and a provable external run bound false. Therefore the normal runner refuses before a provider request. A fake provider or injected gateway cannot authorize paid work.

## Admission requirements before reconsideration

1. Verify exact provider, organization/project/workspace, account tier, model availability, region, billing mode, all linked projects, and other actors using approved account evidence.
2. Use dedicated credentials unavailable to other processes and a dedicated billing scope where the provider supports it.
3. Establish an enforced external spend ceiling whose scope, propagation delay, and worst-case overrun are acceptable for a specifically approved run.
4. Verify exact request identity and all billable dimensions, including input/output, reasoning, cache, tool/grounding, long-context, service-tier, and any modality charges.
5. Prove an upper bound for every admitted attempt and reserve the whole retry/fallback envelope before invocation. Preserve uncertain exposure on cancellation, timeout, and crash.
6. Have the immutable approval artifact signed by a separately controlled trusted approval key, then validate the exact dataset, plan, sample IDs, prompt, models, limits, attempts, and budgets at both preflight and execution.

Until these conditions are met, `max_run_budget_usd` is a local ledger limit only. It must not be represented as a hard provider invoice ceiling, and no pilot cost estimate is a guaranteed maximum.

## Final assessment

- Provider-side bound: **not verified**.
- Project isolation and shared-account exposure: **not verified**.
- Complete billable-token bound: **not supported**.
- Paid approval: **unsigned / `NOT_APPROVED`**.
- Production benchmark paid gate: **blocked**.
- Ordinary application LiteLLM route: code can call upstream when configured without using the benchmark SQLite ledger; its per-request budget path currently refuses because no estimator is configured. This route is outside benchmark admission and must not be described as covered by this ledger.
- Real pilot: **`REAL_PILOT_BLOCKED`**.

Official documentation reviewed 2026-11-22: [OpenAI project spend controls](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9186755-managing-projects-in-the-api-platform), [Anthropic rate and spend limits](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/rate-limits), [Gemini billing limits and delay](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/billing).
